concepts.def: IBDP DT uses analysing, designing, planning, creating, evaluating; iterative loops repeat as understanding develops.
Identifies user needs through observation, interviews and PMI charts; benchmarks against existing solutions.
Quantitative and qualitative criteria covering function, ergonomics, aesthetics, materials, cost, sustainability; agreed before design.
Brainstorming, SCAMPER, mood boards and morphological charts produce divergent ideas; convergence selects strongest concept.
Low-fidelity (paper, foam, cardboard) progresses through mid-fidelity (3D-printed) to high-fidelity working models; feedback drives refinement.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Modelling — a core area of Design Technology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Modelling brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Modelling.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

UK Design Council
Stanford d.school
Frog Design

TRIZ
PMI

mcqs.q: What is FEA used for in product design?
options: Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
Simulating how a product will respond to forces, heat, or vibration before manufacture.
Final exam analysis of student designs.

mcqs.q: Why do designers often use 5th to 95th percentile data instead of just the 50th?
options: Because the 50th percentile is too unreliable.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
Because law requires it.
To accommodate the majority of users rather than just the average.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between CAD and CAM?
options: Because law requires it.
CAD creates digital designs; CAM uses those designs to control manufacturing machines.
CAD is for cars, CAM is for cameras.
They are the same thing with different names.
